summary.text: X-ray diffraction is the change in direction of X-ray beams as they interact with the electrons around atoms, giving a map called a diffraction pattern.
Because crystals are regular arrays of atoms, the waves their electrons scatter cancel out in most directions but add up in a few specific ones.
Max von Laue's observation of it in 1912 confirmed that X-rays are electromagnetic radiation, and William Henry and William Lawrence Bragg then developed the field.

facts.label: Braggs' Nobel Prize
facts.value: Physics, 1915, shared by father and son

items.prompt: Ewald's model of how crystals are built could not be tested by shining ordinary visible light on them. Why not?

options.label: Visible light is absorbed by every crystal
Visible light moves too slowly inside crystals
Its wavelength is far larger than the spacing
Its wavelength is far smaller than the spacing

items.explain: Visible light's wavelength is much larger than the spacing in a crystal; von Laue saw that a shorter wavelength, like that of X-rays, was needed.

items.prompt: When an X-ray strikes an electron in a crystal, much like an ocean wave hitting a lighthouse, what does the electron do?

options.label: Sends out new waves spreading in all directions
Absorbs the X-ray and stops it completely
Bounces it straight back toward its source
Gives it extra energy so it speeds up

items.explain: An X-ray striking an electron produces secondary spherical waves coming from the electron, which is elastic scattering.

items.prompt: Why does a crystal send scattered X-rays out in only a few sharp directions instead of a smooth, even glow?

options.label: The crystal's surface blocks most directions
Only a few atoms scatter X-rays at all
X-rays can only travel along straight rows
Waves from the regular array cancel almost everywhere

items.explain: A regular array of scatterers produces waves that cancel in most directions by destructive interference but add up in a few specific directions.

items.prompt: In 1907 William Henry Bragg argued that X-rays were not the same kind of thing as light. What did the 1912 crystal experiment show?

options.label: X-rays are streams of electrons
X-rays are a form of electromagnetic radiation
X-rays are a kind of sound wave
X-rays cannot pass through crystals

items.explain: Bragg's view proved unpopular, and von Laue's 1912 observation of X-ray diffraction confirmed that X-rays are electromagnetic radiation.

items.prompt: A chemist cannot grow single crystals big enough for a full X-ray study. What can they still do?

options.label: Nothing, since only single crystals scatter X-rays
Use visible light instead for full detail
Use powder diffraction for less detailed results
Heat the sample until it scatters more sharply

items.explain: Without large enough single crystals, methods such as powder or fiber diffraction can still give less detailed information.

items.prompt: In Bragg's model, X-rays reflect off a stack of evenly spaced planes. When do the reflections from neighbouring planes reinforce each other?

options.label: When their path difference is a whole number of wavelengths
When their path difference is half a wavelength
Only when the beam hits the planes at 90°
Whenever the planes are spaced very closely

items.explain: Reflections from adjacent planes add constructively when the angle gives a path-length difference that is an integer multiple n of the wavelength λ.
